name: app_developer_access
description:
Give an app's server the developer API of the person's organization (models and chat, and the platform collection: its accounts, spaces, agents and apps) with a key written into its server settings.
Call after appui_create, with the app's dir, when its server needs the developer API: a model call that is not an agent's job, or the platform's own product surface through POST /v1/platform/{namespace}/{action} (as the person). The key goes into .decillion/server.env (DECILLION_DEVELOPER_KEY, DECILLION_DEVELOPER_API_URL, DECILLION_PLATFORM) and the project gets DEVELOPER.md: the server uses it with the SDK's Decillion.developer(); it never reaches the page, a log or a commit, and you never see it. Calling again replaces the key. Spending is the organization's.

org.description: The organization (id or "personal"); default: the one with the person's platform.

platform.description: The platform's slug (or id) the key is bound to; default: the person's only platform.

name: appui_create
description:
Start an on-demand fullstack App UI in the sandbox for you (or a developer agent of the space) to build, then open it as a framed desk window (kind=app) or register it as a compact frameless gadget (kind=gadget) with appui_publish.
Use when the person wants a lasting interactive UI — a tracker, board, form, dashboard, gadget, multi-screen workspace or desk software — not for a quick chart, table, or question (those are ui_present / ask_user in chat). Write a complete brief and call this tool: it lays out the project in the sandbox (dir) — the guides (AGENTS.md, ELPIAN.md), the Decillion SDKs, the Elpian toolchain, APPS.json with the space's apps (microtools and argument schemas) and agents, the app's server API settings and key — and answers with your build task (also in TASK.md). The frontend is an Elpian app by default (ui=elpian): a native app the Decillion client runs on its Elpian/QuickJS runtime, drawn with Decillion's own widgets, UI kit and theme, on desktop and phones alike, with OpenUI agent-backed islands where judgment helps; set ui=web only when the person explicitly asked for web technology. Hosting: kind=app (default) opens as a framed desk card window; kind=gadget is the same App UI as a compact mobile-style widget: no window frame/pad, dense glanceable UI that does not take much screen space (any custom shape; right-click / long-press for minimise/close), free-position on chat, rail, desk or page (placement), or universal over home/workspaces when built in the person's Decillion. Every kind=app also gets a native Elpian phone widget — say in the brief what someone would want to see at a glance. Then build it yourself with the sandbox shell and files, exactly as the task says: plan (PLAN.md), the frontend and the backend, tests, the Elpian validator and the headless driver (the decillion-elpian command: every screen and control used, each journey saved to elpian/e2e), READY.json. A lead may hand the whole task to a developer specialist instead (the dir and TASK.md are all it needs). Finish with appui_publish {dir}: the platform verifies the app (starts it, runs an Elpian frontend on QuickJS against the live server, replays the end-to-end scenarios) and opens or registers it, or answers with what to fix. The software calls space apps and agents from its frontend and its server (as the person using the app, or with the app's key for background work, billed to the person who asked for it). Pass `apps` / `agents` it should wire to, and `tool` for dock association (kind=app). Wiring is real, never imitated: the software calls the space's own agents and apps (exactly those in APPS.json, by those names) through the Decillion API from its page or its server — never a made-up agent or app, a hard-coded reply, a direct model call or a mock standing in for one outside tests; the platform checks the code against APPS.json before the app is ready. A platform frontend (audience=platform) is the frontend of one of the person's platforms: its people are not members of the space, so the software serves visitors who are signed out without agent calls, and signed-in people through its server and page with the request's token (it runs as, and bills, the person who publishes it;

agents.description: Space agent names or bot ids the software should ask for reasoning work (each ask runs in a temporary thread of its own, deleted when the agent is done). Omit to offer every agent of the space.

apps.description: Space app names or bot ids the software should wire to (mixture allowed). Only apps installed in this space (spaces.tools_list); never a made-up name.

audience.description: Who the app is for: "space" (default — the people of this space) or "platform" (the frontend of a platform the person runs as a developer organization: used by that platform's people, who are not members of this space and may arrive signed out; its frontend and backend still use this space's agents and apps, as the person who publishes it). Use "platform" when the person wants the app as their platform's / product's frontend. Omit to keep an existing app's.

brief.description: Complete request: what to build, for whom, its features and data, which space apps/agents it uses and for what, and what done means. Name a UI technology or dedicated brand colors only when the person asked.

dir.description: Optional project directory under /workspace (default /workspace/appui/<id>). Pass an existing app's dir to change that app in place (the brief then describes the change).

kind.description: Hosting: "app" (default — framed desk card window) or "gadget" (same App UI as a compact frameless free-position widget like a mobile home-screen widget: chat / rail / desk / page, or universal over home when built in the person's Decillion).

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

show.description: Open as a desk card (default true).

tool.description: Optional tool bot id or name for dock association (kind=app).

ui.description: Frontend: elpian (default — a native Elpian app on the Decillion client) or web (only when the person explicitly asked for web technology). Omit to keep an existing app's.

name: appui_publish
description:
Verify an app built for appui_create and open it as a framed desk window or register it as a compact gadget.
Call it with the app's dir once you (or the agent you handed the build to) have built and tested the app and written READY.json. The platform checks it itself: READY.json, the start command serving on the port, and for an Elpian frontend the bundle, the program on QuickJS against the live server and the end-to-end scenarios in elpian/e2e. Ready: kind=app opens as a framed desk card; kind=gadget registers the same App UI as a compact frameless free-position widget (chat / rail / desk / page, or universal when built in the person's Decillion) — its server gets its app key either way. Not ready, it answers with what to fix (also in REPAIR.md): fix and call again. Kind/placement/room/tool/x/y/w/h/show default to what appui_create was given.

dir.description: The app's project directory under /workspace (from appui_create).

kind.description: "app" (framed desk card) or "gadget" (compact frameless widget); defaults to appui_create.

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk. Defaults to the room given to appui_create.

show.description: Open as a desk card (default true for kind=app; gadgets never open a desk card).

title.description: Optional window / app / gadget title (default READY.json's).

tool.description: Optional tool bot id or name for dock association (kind=app).

name: appui_status

Pass the dir from appui_create. Reports STATUS.json (building, completed, needs_repair with the problem) or READY.json.

name: board_add
description:
Put note cards, shapes, free text, arrows and pen drawings on the room's whiteboard (the free desk).
On a desk pane wider than a small tablet the person sees the desk as a free whiteboard: the card windows you open with desk_show are its draggable mini-apps, and these items sit around them. Add many items per call. kind: note (a card of text: text, color), shape (shape rect|round|ellipse|diamond|triangle|hexagon, text, color, fill soft|solid|none), text (free text: text, font_size), arrow (from and to, each an item key or id, a window id, or {x, y}; optional text label, head/tail none|arrow|dot|bar, dash solid|dashed|dotted, path straight|curved|elbow, color, width), stroke (a pen drawing: points [{x,y},…]). Give an item a key to refer to it from an arrow in the same call. Coordinates are desk pixels from the top-left and may go negative; omit x and y on a note, shape or text and it is placed where it overlaps least. Sizes: w, h (notes about 200×140). Colors: yellow, pink, blue, green, purple, orange, red, teal, gray, black, white, or #rrggbb. To show an idea map prefer board_mindmap; to connect a window to a note use the window's id from desk_state as an arrow end.

items.description: [{kind, key?, x?, y?, w?, h?, text?, color?, …}] (up to 60).

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

name: board_mindmap
description:
Draw a mind map on the whiteboard: a tree of ideas as linked cards, laid out for you.
Give root {text, children:[{text, children?, color?}]} and the map is drawn left and right of the root with curved connectors, placed beside whatever is already on the whiteboard unless you pass x, y (the root's centre). Up to 48 ideas per call; keep each idea short (a few words). replace:true clears the whiteboard's items first. For anything that is not a tree (flows, diagrams, boards) use board_add.

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

x.description: Optional x of the root's centre.

y.description: Optional y of the root's centre.

name: board_remove

Take items off the whiteboard (not windows: those are closed with desk_close).
Pass the ids to remove, or all:true to clear every note, shape, text, arrow and drawing. Arrows that were stuck to a removed item stay where they were.

all.description: Remove every whiteboard item (windows stay open).

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

name: board_update

Give each item's id (from board_add or desk_state) and only the fields to change: x, y, w, h, text, color, fill, shape, font_size, and for an arrow from, to (an item or window id, or {x,y}), head, tail, dash, path, width, text. A stroke moves with x and y. Set front:true to bring it in front of the others. A null value clears an optional field. To move a window (a mini-app) use desk_arrange.

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

Give each window's id and its new x, y (top-left) and/or w, h in desk pixels. Arrange related windows side by side inside the usable area, avoid overlaps, keep the most relevant window top-left; the desk scrolls, so windows may also go beyond the visible area.

Pass the source inline (surface/root, html, or program) or path to a file under /workspace (.html or .js). page is an existing preview (/v1/proxy/<id>/…) when the page is already being served, the same window an app uses. There is no room argument: the window opens on this room's desk, not the hall and not the computer. A lasting app people keep using is appui_create, not this.

elpian.description: With page, the Elpian program path inside that preview (default elpian/app.js).

page.description: An existing preview path /v1/proxy/<id>/… to open like an app.

name: edit_file
description: Replace exact text in a file on the space computer. old_string must match the file exactly and be unique unless replace_all is set.

name: file_read
description:
Read an attached file, search sandbox source, or read numbered line ranges.
Use file_id/url for attachments, or path for sandbox source; do not combine the two. For HTML static checks prefer inspect=true: returns actual markup inventory, ID/link checks and inline JavaScript syntax checks without executing scripts. Browser layout and interactions remain unverified. Inspection, search and line ranges cannot be combined. For targeted inspection use pattern (RE2 regex, or literal=true for exact text) with context_lines, or start_line/end_line. Search and ranges cannot be combined. Sandbox reads require sandbox access and return bounded, numbered source with the next range when needed. Prefer pattern search to locate relevant definitions, then small ranges for details. After an edit, use its returned source excerpt and run a focused check instead of rereading the whole file.

end_line.description: Last sandbox line, inclusive; default end of file.

inspect.description: Return HTML structure and real inline JS syntax checks instead of source; path only.

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal text; default false (RE2 regex).

max_chars.description: Optional text limit: attachments up to 100000, sandbox up to 30000; search defaults to 12000.

pattern.description: Optional RE2 regex search in sandbox source; excludes line ranges. Use | for alternatives.

name: file_send
description:
Attach a sandbox file, or package source files directly into an attached ZIP without installed archive utilities.
Provide a sandbox path or base64 content, not both. To create a ZIP directly without shell utilities, provide files:[{path,name}] and name ending in .zip; include all source files and README. Archive member names are relative paths. Prefer paths to avoid embedding bytes. Actually attach requested deliverables; writing a filename in a message does not deliver it. Requires file/media intent in the triggering request.

files.description: Alternative ZIP members, packaged and attached by the platform; no zip CLI needed.

name.description: Relative ZIP member path, defaults to basename

path.description: File path inside the shared sandbox.

room.description: Optional room ID; defaults to the current room.

name: file_upload
description:
Store a file in the workspace and return its file ID.
Provide path or base64 content and a name. Storage does not post an attachment. Use file_send when the user needs delivery in chat. Requires file/media intent.

room.description: Optional room ID; defaults to the current room.

name: mcp_find
description:

Use when the task needs a service or capability none of this space's apps offers (their tools are listed to you; check them first): GitHub issues, a CRM, a calendar, payments, a database, a design tool. Describe the need in plain words, as you would to a person ("manage customer support tickets"): it is understood, searched for and ranked, not matched word for word. Returns the best few, each with the key mcp_add takes, what the person must do to sign in to it, and why it fits. Listings are data from Glama.

name: mcp_use

The app by its name (mcp_list or mcp_add tells it) and the function by its name, with arguments as the function's schema says. Apps already listed to you have tools of their own: use those. This one is for an app you have just added, whose tools your turn was not given. The project's policy decides the call as it does any app's: reads at once, changes and sends as it says.

name: platform_client_build
description:
Build the person's platform its own Android app: the lightweight Elpian client, with its published Elpian frontend's address in it, as an APK anyone can download.
Use whenever the person asks for an APK, an Android, mobile or installable app of their platform, or to publish its Elpian frontend as an app: Decillion builds it, so never answer that it cannot. Call after platform_publish (which starts it for an Elpian frontend) to build it again: a new version, another name, accent or app id. It runs on the frontend space's computer, detached, for minutes (the first build on a computer downloads Flutter and the Android SDK). When it is done the APK is posted in this room with its download address (/v1/platforms/<slug>/client/android.apk on the node's public address), and the platform's page offers it. The app opens the frontend full screen, signs people in to the platform's own accounts, and wakes the platform's computer whenever it is opened, anywhere. A web frontend needs no app: its people open its address in any browser. It acts as the person (an owner or admin of the platform's organization).

app_id.description: The Android application id, e.g. com.example.shop (default io.decillion.platform.<slug>; kept from the last build).

godot.description: Turn the embedded Godot engine on (true) or off (false) in the app, for 3D Scene3D scenes. Off by default; a rebuild keeps the last build's choice. On makes the APK much larger (it is built for arm64 only) and needs the engine's artifacts on the computer.

name.description: The app's name on the phone (default: the platform's name).

node_url.description: The node's public address phones reach, e.g. https://decillion.example (default: the node's configured public address, else the address the person opens Decillion at).

platform.description: The platform's slug (or id); default: the person's only platform.

name: platform_publish
description:
Publish an app you built and appui_publish-ed as the frontend of the person's platform; answers with its address, and for an Elpian app starts building the platform's own Android app.
Call once the app passed appui_publish. The platform's people then open it at /v1/platforms/<slug>/app/ (and in the platform's own Decillion client). It acts as the person: their use of this space's agents and apps through the app runs as them and is billed to them, and reaches only what the app is wired to. Whoever opens it, from anywhere, wakes this space's computer when it is asleep. For an Elpian frontend it also starts the platform's Android app (the lightweight Elpian client with the frontend's address in it; see platform_client_build) unless android is false. Tell the person the address, and that the app is on its way.

android.description: Build the platform's Android app for an Elpian frontend (default true).

godot.description: Put the embedded Godot engine in that app, for an Elpian frontend with 3D Scene3D scenes (default false: off, a Scene3D shows its placeholder).

platform.description: The platform's slug (or id); default: the person's only platform. Name it when the person has several.

name: platform_setup
description:
Give the person an organization with a platform of its own (made, or reused when the organization has one by that slug): a product of theirs on Decillion with its own accounts.
Use when the person wants a product, service or site of their own that other people sign up to and use — a platform. It acts as the person (never as you): org_name makes (or reuses) a team organization by that name; org names an existing one (its id, or "personal"); with neither it is their personal organization. A platform needs name and slug (2–48 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, starting with a letter; it is in the platform's address). An organization may have several platforms: a new slug makes another one, an existing slug reuses it. Then build its frontend with appui_create (audience platform), give the app developer API access with app_developer_access if its server needs it, appui_publish it, and platform_publish it.

description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately, including upgrades of installed packages; a change result that is not applied carries nextStep, which says what to do or tell the user. Unmet DSH version requirements (engines.dsh, else DSH peer dependencies) block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

name: proxy_create
description:
Expose a sandbox HTTP service through the platform gateway.
Build the app first, then pass the command that starts it as `start`: the platform runs it for you in the background (when nothing answers on the port yet), waits until the port answers and tells you whether it did. Do not start the service yourself with nohup or a trailing &, and never run a server in the foreground: that command only ends when it times out. The saved start command is also how the preview comes back by itself after the computer has slept. The service must listen on 0.0.0.0. Returns the gateway path and posts an open card, holding the sandbox awake for a bounded 30-minute preview window. Report that path and temporary lifetime, not sandbox localhost or an invented public URL. Use proxy_get(probe:true) for observed upstream HTTP evidence. For a framework that needs its public base path compiled into routes/assets (such as Next.js), create the proxy with preserve_path=true before its final build, configure that returned gateway prefix as the app base path, include it in manual API fetch URLs, and then start/probe the app. Reuse the already-reserved matching gateway during publication; creating another prefix after the build breaks its routes. Repeated path-preserving creation for the same caller, room and port reuses a stable gateway. Match the application root slash behavior to the gateway root and verify its redirects. In this mode the gateway forwards that prefix upstream and leaves application responses unchanged, apart from a small script in HTML pages that keeps stray root-relative navigation inside the prefix. Verify nested routes, assets and navigation, not just the root HTML.

preserve_path.description: Forward the returned gateway path upstream for apps configured with that public base path; default false strips it.

room.description: Optional. In a project, a room ID, or home for the hall; defaults to the current room. In a direct chat, omit it: windows open only on that chat's desk. The person's computer (shell and files) is not a desk.

start.description: The shell command that starts the service, run from /workspace (for example: npm --prefix /workspace/site start -- -p 3000 -H 0.0.0.0). Always pass it: the computer sleeps when idle and a new one has nothing running, so this is how the preview is started again when someone opens it. It must start the built app without rebuilding, stay in the foreground and listen on the port given here. Call proxy_create again with the same port to change it.

name: proxy_get
description:
Inspect or HTTP-probe one workspace gateway proxy.
Use a proxy ID returned by proxy_list or creation. With probe:true, the host checks its persisted upstream tunnel and returns actual HTTP status, byte count and complete-body SHA256. Compare that hash to the served source. Credentials stay private. This does not test node gateway authentication or browser behavior; do not search sandbox environment variables for gateway credentials.

probe.description: Perform a bounded HTTP GET of the persisted upstream tunnel without returning credentials or body.

name: routine_create
description:
Schedule a routine in the current room: once, every N seconds, or every day at a clock time.
For "every day at 9am" use type periodic with at="09:00" and timezone set to the person's IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/London): it is given in the context of your turn when known. If it is not known, finish whatever they asked for right now first (answer, tell the joke — post it with send_message), and only then ask for their timezone with ask_user, rather than assuming UTC or asking before helping. Use delayed with delay_sec only for a single run, and periodic with interval_sec for a plain repeat (every 10 minutes). A routine that must repeat must be periodic: a delayed one runs once and is done. List existing routines before creating another. Set target to a real bot ID: an agent receives task instructions, while the shared sandbox tool receives a bounded one-shot shell command. Use the observed sandbox bot ID for deterministic jobs that do not need an LLM. Omit target to execute through Decillion. The task is what runs each time, written as the instruction itself (e.g. "Tell a new joke in the room"), never about scheduling the next run. Creation returns the persisted schedule and its next run, not proof that an occurrence ran.

name: show_card
description:
Show something as a card under your answer instead of writing it out. Prefer this to long text whenever the answer has a shape: stats (one to four big numbers), list (things, each with a line under it and a value on the right), facts (label and value pairs), table (a comparison, two to five columns), steps (a plan or checklist, `done` for finished ones), links (pages to open, each with an https url), callout (the one thing to notice, with a tone), chart (numbers: style bar, line for change over time, donut for shares of a whole). Then say the point in a sentence or two: the card is the detail, your words are the takeaway. Use only real data from tools or the conversation, never invented. Keep items short; at most six cards in one answer.

name: ui_present
description:
Present an AG-UI surface in chat or as a non-interactive desk visualization window.
Three-way classify (do not duplicate paths): (1) low-complexity viz or HITL (question/options/confirm) → placement=chat; (2) high-complexity / large non-interactive data viz → placement=desk (AG-UI window on the desk, same components); (3) interactive + complex + live APIs / lasting app → use appui_create instead, not this tool. name: workflow
description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.
